However, xylitol was found to be ineffective when it was used only during an acute respi- ratory-tract infection38 and the need for use 5 times a day may make this treatment impractical.35,36 Vaccination against AOM with pneumococcal vaccines has also been tried but unconjugated multivalent polysac- charide vaccines do not prevent AOM in children under 2 years of age23,39 and their benefit in older children is min- imal.39 A meta-analysis39 found that starting immunisation with the 7-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine by 2 months of age reduces the incidence of recurrent AOM. No benefit was noted in children with recurrent infections who received their first vaccination after 1 year of age. In a later study40 in children 2 to 8 years of age with recurrent OME, vaccination with the 7-valent conjugated vaccine before, and the 23-valent polysaccharide vaccine after, in- sertion of a tympanostomy tube did not prevent recurrenc- es. Vaccination may also have a role in reducing the incidence and in preventing the development of antibacterial resistance23 but use of conjugated pneumococcal vaccines was found to cause a shift in the pathogens responsible for AOM from vaccine-type pneumococci to nonvaccine-type strains and to H. influenzae.23 1.
